The Fermi level in (Ga,Mn)N layers with Mn concentration x > 0.1% is located about 1.25 - 1.55 eV above the valence band edge.
The Fermi level in (Ga,Mn)N is strongly pinned in the middle of the band gap, with a negligibly small surface depletion layer.
The majority of the band gap change in (Ga,Mn)N takes place in the valence band, amounting to a decrease of 0.028 ± 0.008 eV per % of Mn.
The strong mid-gap Fermi level pinning, high resistivity, and lack of a surface depletion layer make (Ga,Mn)N an excellent insulating buffer material for GaN-based devices.
For (Ga,Mn)N samples with Mn concentration x < 0.1%, the Fermi level is located closer to the conduction band edge, similar to the Fermi level position at the GaN surface.
The paper used contactless electroreflectance (CER) spectroscopy to analyze the built-in electric field in a GaN cap layer grown on the (Ga,Mn)N layers.
The period of the Franz-Keldysh oscillations in the CER spectra was used to determine the Fermi level position in the (Ga,Mn)N layers.
The (Ga,Mn)N layers studied in this paper were grown by molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) and had Mn concentrations ranging from 0.1% to 7%.
The structural and chemical characterization of the samples was performed using X-ray diffraction, secondary ion mass spectrometry, and superconducting quantum interference device magnetometry.
The authors used single (Ga,Mn)N layers as reference samples to support their study of the bilayer GaN/(Ga,Mn)N structures.
